summary: Broker drops the socket: the manager reconnects, sends connect again, waits for ck and subscribes the touchline and the depth feed again; the new acknowledgement and an update come through.

notes: The desktop clears its snapshots on every connect (streaming.rs on_connected); the web keeps them across a reconnect (_on_close / _resubscribe_all clear nothing), which only shows if an update came before the new acknowledgement. Here the acknowledgement comes first, as Definedge answers a subscribe.

No frame carries the depth feed's `ltt` (an IST HH:MM:SS): the desktop reads it on the IST day the tick arrives (streaming.rs clock_on_day_of), so its epoch-ms value depends on the day the case runs and cannot be pinned here; brokers::definedge::tests::quote_feed::a_depth_message_carries_the_full_quote_and_the_trade_time pins it. Without it both sides take the feed time `ft` (epoch seconds) as the trade time.

deviations.reason: The web forwards Definedge's raw time as ltt: the feed time `ft` in epoch seconds (or the depth feed's clock text HH:MM:SS), a wrong value where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md); it is a JSON string as well. The desktop sends the epoch ms value.

Definedge's web adapter sends the percent change only (change_percent, percent_change), never price_change, for any instrument; the desktop adds its canonical price_change. Lead rules 2026-11-09: change keys outside the docs follow the adapter; dropped in Phase B through the per-broker switch.

Definedge's web adapter names the percent change change_percent and percent_change (both sent by the desktop too); the desktop adds its canonical price_change_percent. Dropped in Phase B through the per-broker switch (lead rules 2026-11-09).
